answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a stake that is slowly earned, not bought: reputation accrues like a marble dropped into a jar, one verified voyage at a time, so a fresh identity starts with nothing. New agents must complete small, peer-reviewed jobs before they can hold ivory-tier privileges such as large payments or voting. Creating thousands of fake identities then costs thousands of real work histories, making the attack far more expensive than any reward it could extract.
